classLaw.code: The language has the section 6.3 body spans - function, method, closure/lambda, impl item and block bodies - and a published L2/L3 normalisation table. Bears clone body identity (clones@normalized-body-hash) and the code-construct syntax relations (declares/literal/control-flow @ syntactic). Its languageId MUST be a member of foundation body-language-version.languageId, because that identifier enters the clone preimage.
classLaw.data-document: A bundled grammar for a data or document format. It has no section 6.3 body spans, and this kit publishes no tokenisation, literalKind mapping or normalisation law for it. Its files are grammar-only MEMBERS - accounted, inventoried, never unsupported-file - bearing file/package/vcs-change inventory evidence under the syntax universe. It mints NO body identity, no suffix of it appears in the syntax dialect table, and its languageId MUST NOT be in body-language-version.languageId. A clone or code-construct request against it is explicitly UNAVAILABLE (language-tier-unsupported for that capability), never a complete empty clone result, which would read as a finding of no clones.

law.boundaries: This registry is the authority at THREE boundaries, not one. (1) Grammar-bundle admission: a row's declared syntaxClass must equal the registered one, in both directions. (2) Every admitted fact2 under a syntax universe: every ANCHOR PATH must be read by a SELECTED grammar whose capability set contains that relation@rung. (3) Every requested subject-scope under a syntax universe, INCLUDING an empty view: judged on the committed examined extent, where a code capability needs at least one extent path read by a selected code grammar, and a capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable. INVENTORY CAPABILITIES (file@enumerated, package@manifest-declared, vcs-change@vcs-reported) are ALWAYS available and are never grammar-gated at boundary (2) OR boundary (3). An earlier revision stated that exemption only inside boundary (3), and boundary (2) read as an unconditional every-anchor rule; a literal implementer therefore refused the very inventory facts boundary (3) had just promised were unconditionally available, which made an inventoried .py path inventoriable and unrepresentable at the same time. The exemption belongs to both because it is a property of the RELATION, not of the boundary: an inventory fact is not read by a grammar at all - it is the snapshot inventory row, the manifest declaration or the VCS observation - so there is no grammar for it to be gated on. Independently of this exemption the relation registry anchorLaw closes the inventory class at ZERO anchors, so an inventory fact names no anchor path for boundary (2) to test in the first place; the two laws agree and neither depends on the other. An earlier revision enforced only (1), which constrains what a bundle says about itself and not what a Run claims: Markdown declares facts, complete empty declares/clones Coverage and references@resolved-binding under resolutionAttempted=false all admitted. None of the three consults a claimed coverage value, a caller-declared class, or whether facts exist.
law.inventoryIsNotGrammarGated: Normative. A snapshot inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads, so requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow the promise this registry makes. The three inventory capabilities are therefore exempt at every boundary this registry owns, on every path - unsupported suffix, extensionless, data-document and code alike - and a `vcs-change` on a `deleted` path that is not in the snapshot at all. This is an exemption from GRAMMAR OWNERSHIP only. It does not exempt an inventory fact from its relation's snapshot joins (path in the inventory; for `file` also the content digest, the byte length and custody of the retained bytes), from own-scope attribution, or from the anchorLaw; and it does not make a CODE fact admissible merely because some other anchor of the same Run is on a supported path.
law.unavailableRequestDisclosure: A well-formed request for a capability this universe cannot serve is DISCLOSED, not answered and not refused outright: coverage `unknown`, deficiency `language-tier-unsupported`, nativeCause `capability-missing` - existing vocabulary, mapped in native-evidence section 10. A false `complete`, a wrong or null cause and a wrong deficiency each refuse with their own typed reason. The capability is retained: a data-grammar inventory Run and a code-grammar declares/clones Run still close with a genuine complete and no deficiency.
law.selectionMatters: An UNSELECTED grammar lends no capability. Selection is committed in the universe identity, so a bundle that ships a grammar the universe did not select cannot make its capabilities available.

syntaxClassIsNotCallerSelected: Normative and CLOSED. The per-language capability mapping of the bundled grammar set, published here so a consumer can reconstruct it without reading author code. syntaxClass is NOT caller-selected: a grammar row declaring a class other than the one this registry assigns to its languageId is refused at grammar-bundle admission, in both directions.
bodyAndNormalizerLaw: A normalized clone body identity is admissible only where the SELECTED grammar bundle retains a normalizer specification whose level applies to that grammar; the L0 level is byte-span only and needs no normalizer. The data-document class in this kit carries no clones capability, so a normalized body level is not merely unused there -- it is unavailable, and the honest record is the published unavailability pairing, never a complete-empty clones result.
